title: dependability-interop-roadmap-and-ops-sprint-notes
content:
Purpose and intent:
This doc captures the cross-functional runway and short-term sprint plan to integrate service-level objectives (SLOs) into model-serving flows across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to produce a repeatable, minimal-risk rollout pattern we can hand to feature teams and platform partners, plus an ops sprint backlog that lets SREs and platform engineers validate telemetry, incidentables, and rollback triggers in a staged fashion.

Context and why now:
- Recent incidents highlighted gaps between model-serving metrics (KV cache pressure, batch tail latency) and product-facing SLOs.
- Platform must support: per-model latency SLOs, error-rate SLOs (user-visible failures), and model-quality guardrails (regression alerts).
- Product deadlines: Hosted API scaling for Q2 launches; Dedicated contracts require SLA templates.

Primary objectives (30/60/90):
- 30d: Define canonical SLO templates, minimal signal set, and decision matrix for rollback vs graceful degradation. Produce instrumented test harness for synthetic load.
- 60d: Run two canary experiments (one hosted, one dedicated) with automated KV prefix caching and dynamic batching engaged; validate alert fidelity and playbook run times.
- 90d: Hand off SLO-onboarding kit (README + Runbook + Dashboard template + Linear/JIRA checklist) to two product teams and one enterprise pilot.

Scope (in-scope / out-of-scope):
- In-scope: model-serving request path (router -> runtime -> GPU pools), per-route and per-model SLO definitions, observability dashboards, runbooks, oncall playbooks, and release gating for canaries.
- Out-of-scope: model training pipeline changes, external customer SLAs (we provide templates but customer legal negotiation is separate).

Stakeholders and responsibilities:
- Platform Engineering (owner): orchestrate rollout, gating, capacity/backpressure knobs.
- Serving Runtime (owner): expose latency percentiles, batching queues, KV cache evictions, and safe-fail modes via telemetry.
- Site Reliability (owner): SLO definition, alert thresholds, runbooks, and incident analysis.
- Observability (support): dashboard templates, tracing hooks, synthetic monitors.
- Product (consumer): validate UX degradation modes and acceptance criteria.
- Solutions Eng / Customer Success (pilot): run customer-facing pilot and gather feedback.

Key signals (minimal signal set) to feed SLOs and alerts:
- p50/p90/p99 end-to-end latency (per-route, per-model variant)
- request success rate (HTTP 2xx vs 5xx, upstream errors, rate-limited events)
- tail GPU queue length and batch size distribution
- KV cache hit ratio and eviction rate (prefix match %)
- synthetic request latency from regional probes
- model-quality regression score (eval prompt set) — asynchronous alert

Decision rules and rollback triggers (draft):
- Immediate rollback if user-visible error rate > 0.5% for 5m for a core route AND p99 latency > 2x baseline for same period.
- Gradual throttle if batch tail latency increases > 30% but success rate unchanged; engage degraded resampling (drop nonessential tokens) after operator confirmation.
- Fall back to smaller model variant automatically if throughput drops below SLO and precious capacity cannot be provisioned within 10 minutes.

Experiment matrix (canary plan):
- Canary A: Hosted API, region us-west-2, 2% traffic ramp, enable KV caching + dynamic batching, monitor for 48h. Owner: Mateo
- Canary B: Dedicated pool, internal test-org, synthetic traffic at 60% of commit throughput, test autoscaler and fallback to q4 quantized model. Owner: Rina
- Success criteria: no P1s, alert precision > 80% (true positives), false positive rate < 5%, dashboards show stable p99 within 1.5x baseline.

Sprint breakdown (6 sprints, 2-week sprints):
- Sprint 1 (week 1–2): Finalize SLO templates, map signals to metrics, implement synthetic harness. Tasks: telemetry schema draft, dashboard stub, linear tickets.
- Sprint 2 (week 3–4): Instrument runtime to emit batch and KV metrics, wire synthetic probes to observability. Tasks: add metrics exporters, trace hooks.
- Sprint 3 (week 5–6): Implement rollback and fallback automation in router; create canary gating automation. Tasks: safety checks, feature flags.
- Sprint 4 (week 7–8): Run Canary A; iterate on alert thresholds and runbooks. Tasks: incident drills, runbook dry-runs.
- Sprint 5 (week 9–10): Run Canary B; capacity stress test and autoscaler tuning. Tasks: scaling plays, fallback verification.
- Sprint 6 (week 11–12): Compile onboarding kit, finalize docs, handoff to product pilots. Tasks: finalize templates, training session.

Communications and ops cadence:
- Weekly cross-functional sync (15m): status, blockers, decisions; rotate facilitator (Platform lead).
- Canary-day war room: invite SRE, runtime, observability, product; use #ops-canary channel for real-time logs.
- Postmortem window: 48h for P1/P0, 5 business days for P2s.

Runbook outlines (for engineers oncall):
- Play 1: High tail latency on Model-Serving Router
  - Detect: p99 > threshold for 5m, correlated with GPU queue length > X
  - Immediate actions: toggle canary flag, scale down batch size, enable degraded output mode
  - Escalation: notify oncall SRE and platform owner, open incident ticket REL-
- Play 2: Elevated 5xx errors
  - Detect: >0.5% error rate for 5m OR >1% for 1m on core route
  - Immediate actions: cut traffic to canary cohort, switch to fallback model variant, increase logging level

Ownership matrix (RACI style):
- Telemetry schema: R(platform), A(observability), C(serving-runtime), I(SRE)
- Canary automation: R(platform), A(platform), C(serving-runtime, SRE)
- Runbook creation: R(SRE), A(SRE), C(platform, product)

Open questions / risks (notes for leadership):
- Threshold calibration: do we have enough historical telemetry to set p99 SLOs for novel models? Short-term: use synthetic baselines, plan to iterate.
- Model-quality integration: how fast can model regression alerts be trusted to gate rollouts? Current eval throughput is slow.
- Capacity costs: autoscaler aggressiveness increases cost — need finance signoff for pilot budgets.

Action items (first 14 days):
- Aisha: publish SLO template doc and share with product & SRE (due 2026-01-18).
- Mateo: deliver synthetic harness (k6 + local mock runtime) and test scripts (due 2026-01-22).
- Rina: prototype KV cache telemetry exporter into observability (due 2026-01-25).
- Connor: draft canary channel setup and war room play (due 2026-01-20).

Appendix: quick references and useful links
- Example dashboards: link to drafts in observability (internal)
- Related tickets: REL-621 (SLO templates), REL-709 (canary automation), PLAT-1183 (router fallback)
- Useful commands: curl health checks, trace-map queries (examples in Confluence)

Notes to self / informal scratchpad:
- Keep the first canary deliberately small and reversible.
- Push for feature-flagged rollout tools rather than ad-hoc scripts.
- Consider a lightweight cost-alert that notifies product when autoscaler-driven spend increases >20% over baseline.
- Training idea: 1-hour deep-dive for product PMs + runbook tabletop after Sprint 4.

Document history and edits:
- 2026-01-15 created by Aisha Patel (initial outline)
- 2026-01-20 Mateo added canary harness notes and experiment owners
- 2026-02-10 Rina updated telemetry fields and sprint dates

This is a working doc — please add comments inline, tag owners on unresolved items, and link PRs when metric exports are available.
